We compute PEX consistency score using the language model M (e | Q(q, a)) and M (e | Q(q, ¬a)), treating the model as a judge of how well an explanation supports the prediction versus its negation.

While human evaluation is valuable, it is prohibitively expensive at scale, and may be confounded by humans' preconceived notions—especially when conflating explanation faithfulness with plausibility. While language models also reflect biases, they offer a consistent and scalable means of evaluation.
